question: Does the official DS1525+ V1500B firmware provide a useful control for adapting DS1522+ to V1500B before another costly CPU replacement?
answer: Yes. The comparison corroborates specific existing CPU support and board-policy mechanisms, but it does not establish a transplantable image or a verified V1500B boot on DS1522+.
current_judgment: No specific missing V1500B basic-initialization prerequisite was identified. Board topology remains the strongest concrete working hypothesis; it is not proven to be the sole cause.
observed_shared_behavior: The actual family/package matcher and candidate-selection block in AmdSocFp5RvPei are byte-identical.
All eight PMU memory-training code/data entry extents are byte-identical; three of four CPU microcode entries are identical.
Both BIOSes have executable V1500B power-policy branches and a16W path.
After normalizing PE HIGHLOW image relocations, the selected CPM Init/GPIO Init/PCIe Init PEIM text sections are byte-identical.
The relevant device-reset table and its lookup behavior are the same; no extra mandatory reset mapping for the candidate was demonstrated.
meaningful_differences: PSP, SMU, ABL and other code/configuration are not all identical; newer labels alone do not prove that DS1522 lacks a required CPU feature.
DS1522 has four1GbE onboard ports and eSATA expansion; DS1525 has two2.5GbE ports and USB Type-C expansion.
DS1525 uses six active platform0 PCIe roots with different logical lanes/BDF assignments; the DS1522 candidate uses the five DS1522 roots and clock rows.
The DS1522 candidate separates logical lanes0 and1 into x1 PCIe links, while DS1525 combines them as x2. Actual V1500B training of the candidate combination remains unobserved.
candidate_decision: The comparison alone does not demonstrate a mandatory change to the existing130-byte topology/clock candidate. Retain DS1522 board-specific wiring, clocks, reset policy and current mutable configuration.
readiness: HOLD_CPU_REWORK: candidate deployment/restore, boot on the installed R1600, physical serial capture, and exact V1500B lane-allocation validation remain outstanding.

lane_split_followup.same_generation_corroboration: Official Advantech V1000 board diagram shows separate GPP x1 paths, but it does not publish the exact Raven logical-to-physical mapping or list V1500B.
lane_split_followup.remaining: Validate the exact logical0/1 split, full candidate lane set, and resulting root-port assignment under V1500B SMU behavior. The mapper accepting unique requested BDF values is insufficient.
